compiled_state.description:
# Decide the provider qualifier by registry membership, not prefix shape

## Context / Problem

Parent bug `03b0` fixed a real outage-shaped defect: a canonical Bedrock model id
(`anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`) contains a colon in its version suffix, so a
`":" in model` test read it as "already provider-qualified" and silently discarded the operator's
configured `provider = "bedrock"`. That fix shipped a SHAPE test — a pre-colon prefix counts as a
provider only if it matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$` (identifier-like, crucially no dots, since Bedrock
ids are dotted). It lives at `src/rebar/llm/config.py:192` (`_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE`) and is applied
at `src/rebar/llm/config.py:203` inside `split_provider_qualifier`.

The shape test works for the ids we have, but it answers the wrong question. It asks "does this
prefix LOOK like a provider name?" when the answer needed is "IS this prefix a provider name?".
Two consequences are live today, both confirmed by running the tree:

- A typo'd configured provider is accepted at config-resolution time:
  `_resolve_target("claude-opus-4-8", "bedrok")` returns `'bedrok:claude-opus-4-8'`. Config
  resolution runs in `rebar` commands that never reach an LLM, so the mistake is only reported much
  later, at provider construction (`src/rebar/llm/providers.py:180`), if it is reached at all.
- Any future model id whose pre-colon prefix happens to be a lowercase dotless identifier would be
  silently promoted to a "provider". Bedrock ids are dotted today by AWS convention, not by
  contract — the same shape assumption that produced `03b0`.

`03b0` cannot close until this is settled, so it is on the epic's critical path.

The decision (already taken, not reopened here): decide qualification by membership in a known-
provider registry, which is what every comparable project does — LangChain's
`model.split(":", 1)[0] in _BUILTIN_PROVIDERS`, LiteLLM's `model.split("/", 1)[0] in
litellm.provider_list`, pydantic-ai's `infer_provider_class` raising `Unknown provider: …`. The
separator stays `:`.

## Approach

Replace `_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE` with a module-level `frozenset[str]` named `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES`
in `src/rebar/llm/config.py`, and make `split_provider_qualifier` test membership in it.

The set is a literal of plain strings — no imports, no lazy loading, no registry object. This is the
design move LangChain and LiteLLM both make: separate "which names are providers" (a static set of
strings) from "what implements them" (resolved downstream by `ProviderSession`). It fits here for a
concrete reason: `split_provider_qualifier` runs during config resolution, where the optional
`[agents]` extra may not be importable at all, and the `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` module
docstring (lines 27-30) states the constraint the module already lives under — heavy libraries are
imported inside the functions that need them "so `import rebar.llm` stays stdlib-only". A literal
string set satisfies that with nothing lazy to get wrong;
`tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py:51` already enforces the property.

**Contents of the set — 24 names, NO EXCEPTIONS.** Exactly the names
`_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` returns today (`src/rebar/llm/providers.py:54`): `anthropic`,
`bedrock`, `cerebras`, `cohere`, `deepseek`, `gateway/anthropic`, `gateway/bedrock`,
`gateway/google-cloud`, `gateway/groq`, `gateway/openai`, `google`, `google-cloud`, `google-gla`,
`google-vertex`, `grok`, `groq`, `heroku`, `huggingface`, `mistral`, `moonshotai`, `openai`,
`openai-chat`, `vertexai`, `xai`. Verified against the installed runtime: the set difference in
both directions is empty.

rebar's own builder names — `anthropic`, `bedrock`, and `openai` when `base_url` is set
(`src/rebar/llm/providers.py:106` and `:118`) — are all already among those 24, so they add no
name. They are named here because the drift test pins them.

**No name is grandfathered in.** An earlier draft of this plan admitted `google_genai` because the
inference table emits it and a test pinned it. That is rejected. The deciding evidence, from
probing the installed pydantic-ai (1.107.1) directly:

    infer_model("test")                      -> TestModel
    infer_model("test:foo")                  -> ValueError: Unknown provider: test
    infer_model("notaprovider:foo")          -> ValueError: Unknown provider: notaprovider
    infer_model("google_genai:gemini-2.0")   -> ValueError: Unknown provider: google_genai
    infer_model("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8") -> AnthropicModel

Upstream already does exactly what this story proposes — registry membership, hard-rejecting an
unknown provider qualifier — and it rejects BOTH `test` and `google_genai`. `test` is not a
provider in pydantic-ai at all: it is the special bare model string that instantiates `TestModel`.
Granting either name membership would make rebar MORE permissive than the library it wraps, which
is backwards for a thin provider seam. Note also that no member of the 24 contains an underscore;
`google_genai` is not merely unregistered, it does not match the shape real provider names take.

Five members contain a slash (`gateway/anthropic`, `gateway/bedrock`, `gateway/google-cloud`,
`gateway/groq`, `gateway/openai`) and so are REJECTED by today's shape regex. Membership therefore
widens as well as narrows: those names start splitting correctly. That is a fix, not a regression,
and no existing test pins the old rejection.

**Two paths, deliberately different, because they are different questions.**

1. *An inline prefix in a model string* — `split_provider_qualifier` returns `(prefix, rest)` when
   `prefix` is a member, and `(None, model)` otherwise. It does **not** raise on a non-member. This
   is load-bearing: raising on every unrecognized prefix would break the very ids `03b0` fixed,
   because `"anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0".partition(":")` yields the prefix
   `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1`, which is by construction not a provider name. Falling
   back to "not qualified" is the only answer that keeps a colon-bearing model id intact. This
   matches the OpenRouter precedent upstream: strict on a configured provider, permissive on an
   unrecognized inline prefix.

2. *An explicitly configured provider* — `_resolve_target(model, provider)`
   (`src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:224`) validates `provider` against the same set and raises
   `LLMConfigError` naming the offending value and listing the valid ones, before composing
   anything. This is the capability the shape test cannot provide, and the one the motivating
   `bedrok` case needs: the operator's typo is reported where the operator made it, during config
   resolution, instead of surviving into a composed target string.

An inline typo (`bedrok:claude-opus-4-8`) is unchanged by this work: it becomes unqualified, no
inference prefix matches it, `_resolve_target` returns it verbatim, and the existing typed
`LLMConfigError("unknown provider 'bedrok'; registered providers: …")` at
`src/rebar/llm/providers.py:180` fires at construction. Adding a second diagnostic for it here would
duplicate that error, so it is deliberately not added.

**Fan-in consequence: `infer_provider` returns None for a non-member inline prefix.** Because
`infer_provider` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:213`) delegates to `split_provider_qualifier`, dropping
`test` from the set changes its result for a synthetic model double:
`infer_provider("test:FunctionModel")` goes from `'test'` to `None`. `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:596`
stamps `provider=infer_provider(ran_model)` into the usage log, so two existing assertions change.
`None` is the more truthful telemetry — there is no provider behind a `FunctionModel` double, and
`"test"` was a fabricated value produced only by the shape regex accepting an arbitrary identifier.
These are updated to the new expected value, not weakened or deleted. rebar's `test:` fixtures keep
working because they use `FakeRunner`/`_Recorder` and never reach `infer_model`; the strings still
resolve verbatim through `_resolve_target` (no inference prefix matches them), so only the recorded
`provider` field changes.

**Drift.** The static set and the runtime registries can diverge when pydantic-ai adds a provider.
Rather than couple the config layer to the optional package, a test (guarded by
`pytest.importorskip("pydantic_ai")`, the pattern already used at
`tests/unit/test_llm_provider_factory.py:32`) asserts that every name in
`ProviderSession._builders` and every name in `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` is present in
`KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES`. The assertion is one-directional (runtime names are a subset of the static
set) so that a future rebar builder for a name pydantic-ai does not enumerate is not a failure; with
zero exceptions the two sets are in fact equal today, and the exact-24 literal test pins that. A
pydantic-ai upgrade that adds a provider fails that test loudly here, instead of silently in an
operator's config.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — delete `_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE` (line 192), add the
  `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` frozenset, switch the test in `split_provider_qualifier` (line 203) to
  membership, replace the comment block at lines 183-191 that explains the shape rationale, and drop
  the now-unused `import re` (line 39 — line 192 is its only use, so ruff F401 fails otherwise).
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — validate the explicitly configured `provider` in
  `_resolve_target` (line 224) against `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES`; update its docstring, which currently
  cites the shape decision.
- `tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py` — new cases (below), plus ONE existing case updated: the
  `"google_genai:gemini-2.0"  # ...or an underscore` parametrization at line 72 feeds
  `test_an_already_qualified_string_is_returned_unchanged` (line 75), whose line 77 asserts
  `_resolve_target(already, "google_genai") == already`. Under membership that now correctly raises
  `LLMConfigError`. No member of the 24 contains an underscore, so the property that case was
  pinning ("a provider name may contain an underscore") is not true of any real provider. It is
  replaced by a slashed member (`gateway/openai:gpt-4o`), which pins the same structural class — a
  provider name carrying a non-alphanumeric character round-trips — with a name that actually
  exists. `google_genai` gains a new case asserting its NEW behaviour (unqualified), so coverage of
  the string is strengthened, not dropped. Line 79 of that test
  (`_resolve_target(already, None) == already`) passes unchanged for every case including the
  replacement.
- `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py` — line 330 asserts `rows[0]["provider"] == "test"`; becomes
  `is None` per the fan-in consequence above.
- `tests/unit/test_usage_log_failed_calls.py` — line 121 asserts `row["provider"] == "test"` on the
  failure-row path; same change.
- `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` — the comment at lines 43-45 states "`test:` survives
  `split_provider_qualifier` as a provider qualifier", which stops being true. The strings still
  resolve unchanged (no inference prefix matches `test:…`, so `_resolve_target` returns them
  verbatim), so only the comment's reasoning changes, not the assertions.

The fan-in blast radius is exactly those two usage-log files, verified by grep: a
`provider == "test"` assertion appears nowhere else in `tests/`. The three other files carrying
`test:` model literals — `tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_step_model_attribution.py`,
`tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_usage_attribution.py` and
`tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` — contain no `provider` assertion at all.

Out of scope, stated so it is not read as an omission:

- **The bare-name inference table.** `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:169`) maps
  `gemini` to `google_genai`, so `_resolve_target("gemini-2.5-pro", None)` still yields
  `'google_genai:gemini-2.5-pro'`, which no builder and no pydantic-ai name can construct, so it
  dies at `src/rebar/llm/providers.py:180`. This change validates only the EXPLICITLY CONFIGURED
  provider, never the inferred one, so that path is untouched and behaves identically before and
  after. It is a pre-existing defect filed on its own ticket. Validating inferred providers here
  would fold an unrelated bug fix into this change.
- **`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py`** — its `":" in model` splits (lines 101-102) are eval-only
  scoring helpers, not qualification deciders, and `03b0` deliberately left them alone. Unchanged
  here for the same reason.
- **The guard order** — checking an explicitly configured provider before scanning the model string
  at all — already landed in `03b0` and is untouched.
- **Changing the separator.** `:` stays. pydantic-ai's own `KnownModelName` contains two-colon
  entries (`bedrock:anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`), so "provider, first colon, then a
  model name that may itself contain colons" is our runtime's grammar.

## Testing

In `tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py` unless noted.

- **Happy path** — `split_provider_qualifier("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8")` returns
  `("anthropic", "claude-opus-4-8")`; a configured provider composes
  `_resolve_target("claude-opus-4-8", "anthropic") == "anthropic:claude-opus-4-8"`.
- **The existing suite** — every other case in the file (lines 45, 49, 55, 94, 99, 122, 126, 138,
  150 and 156) keeps passing with no edits, including both canonical Bedrock shapes — versioned
  (`anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`) and the unversioned alias. The single edited case is
  the line-72 parametrization documented in Scope.
- **Failure path (the new capability)** — `_resolve_target("claude-opus-4-8", "bedrok")` raises
  `LLMConfigError`; the message contains `bedrok` and at least one valid name.
- **Edge: unknown inline prefix** — `split_provider_qualifier("bedrok:claude-opus-4-8")` returns
  `(None, "bedrok:claude-opus-4-8")` and does not raise.
- **Edge: dotted multi-colon prefix** — `split_provider_qualifier("anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-
  20251001-v1:0")` returns `(None, <the whole id>)`, the property that makes path 1 safe.
- **Edge: a slashed member** — `split_provider_qualifier("gateway/openai:gpt-4o")` returns
  `("gateway/openai", "gpt-4o")`, the case the shape regex rejected.
- **The two de-registered names** — `split_provider_qualifier("test:FunctionModel")` and
  `split_provider_qualifier("google_genai:gemini-2.0")` each return `(None, <the whole string>)`,
  and `infer_provider` returns `None` for both. This pins the decision that neither name is
  grandfathered.
- **Back-compat enumeration** — a parametrized case over every one of the 24 names asserting
  `split_provider_qualifier(f"{name}:some-model") == (name, "some-model")`.
- **Drift** — the `importorskip`-guarded subset test described in Approach.
- **Fan-in** — `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py` and `tests/unit/test_usage_log_failed_calls.py` assert
  the recorded `provider` is `None` for a `FunctionModel` double.
- **No new optional import** — `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py` continues to pass unchanged,
  which is what proves the set imported nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE` no longer exists anywhere in the tree; verified by
      `! grep -rq "_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE" src/ tests/` exiting 0.
- [ ] Neither decider module re-introduces a raw colon test; verified by
      `! grep -rq '":" in model' src/rebar/llm/config.py src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` exiting 0
      (scoped to the two decider modules — `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:101-102` legitimately
      contains that substring and is out of scope).
- [ ] `_resolve_target` and `infer_provider` each still call `split_provider_qualifier` (they do
      today at `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:239`/`:251` and `src/rebar/llm/config.py:213`).
